summary: MoonGuard, takes players through an interactive 2D game where they respond to emergency challenges, each presented with trade-offs, that teaches young users the problem-solving skills needed on a lunar base while maintaining a fun and easy gaming experience.
details: MoonGuard takes players to a lunar base that is separated into blocks to represent different rooms as a simplification for young users. Rooms include: Greenhouse, Living Quarters, Lab, and Control Room, When the character enters a room, they are provided with a set of tasks to complete and an emergency challenge to respond to. They have a set of the water, power, and oxygen supply percentages that are affected by the emergency challenge trade-offs. The tasks are completed by clicking on each task and its description. Emergency challenges include: Solar radiation, Crop failure, power generator malfunction, and moonquake affects. Each challenge gives the player a set of decisions with descriptions on what life support supplies it affects. The game provides an understandable way for young players ages 7-12 to explore the tasks, systems, emergencies, and trade-offs that occur on lunar missions. We used HTML, CSS, Javascript, and Python as our coding language, and created the game on Visual Studio Code and Github. Instead of having a difficult layout, MoonGuard uses descriptions and buttons to provide users with a more educational experience. Our team took into consideration each team member's coding experience, and for the game itself, we took into consideration user age, simplicity, and educational value.
